subject: Phased commit ascend: proposed month-by-month uplift and fallback rates
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@parcelly.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Phased commit ascend proposal

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. As discussed, Parcelly is at a point where a higher reserved commit will materially reduce per-token costs while giving predictable throughput for your burstier weekends. Attached is a first-draft phased plan (proposal-phased-commit-v1.pdf) and a short usage snapshot for Q2 (usage-report-q2.csv).

High level recommendation (one-page):
- Effective start: Aug 1, 2028 (pro-rata for July if you want a partial month).
- Phase 1 (month 1): +40% hosted commit vs current baseline — light uplift to stabilize routing.
- Phase 2 (month 2): +60% commit — more aggressive throughput as traffic normalizes.
- Phase 3 (month 3+): Full commit target (x units) with standard rate bands.
- Soft-fallback: automatic rate-limited throttle at 95% of committed tokens to protect SLA; hard fallback to regional hosted variant only if sustained over 24h.

Questions for you:
1) Can procurement accept a 90-day ramp window vs instant commit?
2) Any required legal/finance PO wording (we can add a one-line amendment for pro-rata month)?

If you’re comfortable with the structure I’ll: 1) send an internal pricing confirmation, 2) attach a DocuSign packet, and 3) schedule a one-hour ops kickoff (routing/keys/quota).

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: proposal-phased-commit-v1.pdf (pdf), usage-report-q2.csv (csv)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@parcelly.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@parcelly.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased commit ascend proposal

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for sending this over. A few quick items from our side:
- Can you confirm how pro-rata will be calculated for July if we start Aug 1st but want a partial July buffer?
- In month 1 we may still spike due to a marketing push; is there a way to set a temporary burst allowance (paid) above Phase 1 without immediately switching to Phase 2?
- Procurement looped me in on contract language — they prefer explicit monthly billing lines rather than a single composite line item.

I’ve CC’d procurement so they see the doc. I’ll get back with usage confirmations by Monday.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, Parcelly
alex.chen@parcelly.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Phased commit ascend proposal (internal pricing notes)

Team — internal notes after Alex’s reply (procurement CC’d externally). He asked about pro-rata and a temporary paid burst in month 1. My recommendation below:

Proposal refinement (internal):
- Pro-rata: charge a daily pro-rata based on the committed monthly unit price; for July we pro-rate at day-level and invoice with July month-end. Keep language as "pro-rated start charge" in amendment.
- Temporary burst: offer a paid burst pool (one-time top-up credit) rather than increasing the committed tier mid-month. Example: +20% burst pool available for first 30 days billed at on-demand rate *1.1. This protects the commit economics.
- Fallback policy: implement soft-throttle at 95% commit; if sustained >95% for 6 hours, notify customer and auto-scale to the regional hosted variant (charge differential applies). Only escalate to hard fallback after 24h continuous breach.
- Billing format: split lines in SOW — monthly committed units + optional burst credit line item. Procurement asked for explicit monthly lines; this satisfies them.

Action items:
- Vanessa: update proposal PDF to include the burst pool table and explicit line-item billing. (kpi: updated pdf by Mon EOD)
- Dev: prepare ops-runbook summary on fallback mechanics (webhook + throttle thresholds) — include a one-page runbook for their SREs.
- Karthik: sign off on discount tiers for month 1 & 2 (suggested effective blended discount: month1 8% off list, month2 12% off list, full rate thereafter).

Link to deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7890 — add notes after you update.

Hannah

Subject: Re: Phased commit ascend proposal — agreed next steps

Hi Alex / Procurement —

Following internal alignment, thank you for the quick turnaround. Summary of what we agreed and next actions:

Agreed structure:
- Effective start date: Aug 1, 2028 (we will pro-rate July as "pro-rated start charge" on the first invoice).
- Phase 1 (Aug): +40% committed units vs baseline; temporary paid burst pool available for first 30 days (up to +20% at on-demand +10% premium).
- Phase 2 (Sep): +60% committed units (move to blended discount of 12% off list for that month).
- Phase 3 (Oct+): Full target commit and standard rate bands.
- Fallback: soft-throttle at 95% utilization; auto-notify + move to regional hosted variant for sustained >6h; hard fallback only after 24h sustained breach.

Next steps / owners:
- Procurement: confirm preferred PO wording for "pro-rated start charge" and monthly line-item split.
- Alex: confirm you want DocuSign for this packet (link below). If yes we will route for signature and then schedule an ops kickoff.
- Van/Dev/Karthik: finalize attachments and runbook; I will upload updated proposal to the HubSpot deal.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/link/packet/XYZ123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7890

If procurement confirms wording I’ll fire the DocuSign tonight so we can get signatures early next week.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
